BEFORE:

 HON'BLE MRS. DR. MONIKA MALIK , MEMBER

FOR THE COMPLAINANT: M/s Mechman Motors

DATED: 28/10/2026
 ORDER
M. P. STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION,

 PLOT NO.76, ARERA HILLS, BHOPAL

 CONSUMER COMPLAINT NO. 22 OF 2010

 FILED ON 15.07.2010

 DECIDED ON 28.10.2026
M/S MECHMAN MOTORS PVT. LIMITED

(A COMPANY REGISTERED UNDER THE

PROVISIONS OF COMPANIES ACT)
 REGISTERED OFFICE AT- NH-12,

HOSHANGABAD ROAD, MISROD, BHOPAL (M.P.) ... COMPLAINANT.
VERSUS
1. THE NATIONAL INSURANCE CO.LTD.
THROUGH ITS CHAIRMAN,

 REGISTERED & HEAD OFFICE AT

 3, MIDDLETON STREET, KOLKATA 700 071
2. THE BRANCH MANAGER,

 NATIONAL INSURANCE CO.LTD.
BRANCH OFFICE AT 38, BHADBHADA ROAD,

 OPPOSITE G.T.B.COMPLEX, T.T.NAGAR,

 BHOPAL (M.P.) ... OPPOSITE PARTIES

BEFORE :

 HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE SUNITA YADAV : PRESIDENT
 HON'BLE DR. MONIKA MALIK : MEMBER

COUNSEL FOR PARTIES:
Shri Jagdish Ahirwar, learned counsel for the complainant.
Shri Deepesh Shukla, learned counsel for the opposite party.
ORDER

 (Passed On 28.10.2026)

Per Say Justice Sunita Yadav, President:
This complaint has been filed under
Section 17
of the Consumer Protection Act,
1986 (for short 'Act').
-2-
2. Brief facts of the case as stated by the complainant are that the complainant is a
Private Limited Company under the provisions of
Companies Act, 1956
and is engaged in

business of sale and repair of passenger cars of Tata Motors and Fiat. The complainant
company has a showroom and workshop at National Highway No.12, Hoshangabad Road,
Misrod, Bhopal. The complainant company retained the stock i.e. passenger cars, spare

parts etc. in the insured premises for sale and repair work. It is submitted by the complaint
that for safety of its premises and the stocks of all kinds of vehicles, the complainant had
obtained 6 different policies from the opposite party-insurance company under which the

sum insured is as follows:
1. Total sum insured for New Vehicle Stocks Rs.7.15,00,000/-.
2.Total sum insured for Customer Vehicle Stocks Rs.25,00,000/-
3. Total Sum Insured for Electric Inst. Rs.15,00,000/-
4. Total Sum Insured for Furniture/Sanitary and Electrical Fittings
 Rs.2,10,00,000/-
5. Total Sum Insured for Building- Rs.3,50,00,000/-
6. Total Sum Insured for Spares, Lubricate, Oil & Tools- Rs.60,00,000/-
7. Total Sum Insured for Computers/Printers/Laptops Rs.2,00,000/-
-3-
3. It is submitted by the complainant that on 06.02.2010, the employees of
Municipal Corporation, Bhopal damaged the premises illegally and also damaged the

passenger cars, show room, laptops and also take away the valuable articles (insured) from
the premises. The complainant lodged FIR at Misrod Police Station which was registered at
Crime No.72/2010. Thereafter, the complainant after due verification and inspection also

lodged an additional report dated 05.03.2010 to the police authorities. It is submitted by the
complainant that at the time of incident, 143 passenger cars (131 new cars and 12 cars of
customers and visitors) were parked in the premises and the culprits have damaged 35

vehicles hence, the complainant company suffered loss of Rs.34,00,000/-. It is submitted by
the complainant that the culprits have also damaged the furniture including glass fittings and
took away the valuable insured articles i.e. 3 music systems (JBC), 2 Car Bear Lans, 2
 Fridge, 11 pieces Nano mobiles, 4 Laptop, etc. hence the complainant company suffered
loss of Rs.7,00,000/-
4. It is further submitted by the complainant that the complainant company suffered
a total loss of Rs.41,00,000/- in the incident, hence the complainant-company submitted
aforesaid loss to the opposite party-insurance company along with necessary documents

and bills. It is submitted
-4-
by the complainant that the aforesaid premises was duly diverted for commercial purpose by

the order of SDO T.T.Nagar and the Municipal Corporation, Bhopal has also sanctioned the
map and therefore the complainant constructed the building accordingly. It is further
submitted that the opposite party-insurance company after due verification and inspection

issued the policies as mentioned above and therefore the opposite party-insurance
company is liable to pay the amount of loss.
5. It is further submitted by the complainant that on being made claim along with

requisite documents, the opposite party-insurance company vide letter dated 16.04.2010
repudiated the claim stating that the Municipal Corporation has declared the premises
illegal. It is submitted by the complainant that the premises were duly insured by the

insurance company and therefore the opposite party-insurance company is liable to pay the
loss suffered by the complainant in a sum of Rs.41,00,000/-, however, the insurance
company have failed to pay the amount as claimed and therefore, this act of the opposite

party-insurance company comes under the purview of deficiency in service and the
complainant is entitled to get compensation. The complainant is therefore filed the present
complaint alleging deficiency in
-5-
service on part of the opposite party-insurance company seeking total compensation of

Rs.51,00,000/- with interest @ 12 % p.a.
6. The complainant has filed affidavit of its Managing Director, Pragati Agrawal
along with documents as per list in support of her contentions.
7. The opposite party-insurance company has failed to file reply/written statement
within prescribed time limit, therefore their right to file reply was closed vide order dated

08.02.2012. However, the opposite party has filed affidavit of Mukesh Goyal, Divisional
Manager, Officer in charge and duly authorized person, Divisional Office No.II, Bhopal and
affidavit of Santosh Kaithal, Investigator appointed by the insurance company (Page no. 160

to 168) along with set of documents as per list (Page no.169 to 278).
8. In the affidavit, it is submitted that the act of Municipal Corporation cannot be
treated as an illegal act and their act cannot be challenged here in their absence. It is further

stated that prior to FIR of complainant, one FIR is lodged by Municipal Corporation against
complainant and his employees bearing Crime No.71/10 at Misrod Police Station under
Sections 294
,
353
,
332
,
506
,
427
/
34
of IPC but complainant willfully with
-6-
malaise intention hide this fact only to get undue advantage of law, hence the complaint is

liable to be dismissed.
9. It is further stated that as per set principle of insurance, the insurance company
appointed Mr. N. K. Gupta & Co. for assessment of loss of the complainant but it is

important to mention that any loss which occurred due to gross negligence is not covered
under the insurance policy. It is further stated that according to the employees and record of
Municipal Corporation, Bhopal said premise was having illegal construction and loss claimed

by the complainant is the outcome of the act of the Municipal Corporation while discharging
their duties and according to law such outcome of losses are not covered in insurance
contract.
10. It is further stated that according to law, contract of insurance was void Ab-Initio
and any loss which is result of any legal action by local authorities and due to gross
negligence is not covered under the insurance coverage (policy), hence the allegation of

deficiency in service is not sustainable in eye of law. There is no legal infirmity in denying the
loss which is result of any government action in respect to abolition of any unlawful premise
after following the procedure.
-7-
11. It is further stated that according to investigation and survey conducted by the

authorized surveyor of insurance company come to the knowledge that prior to taking any
strict action against the insured, government agency also sent many reminders to the
insured for removing encroachment from complainant's premises and requested them to

demolish the illegal structure but when the complainant willfully continuously ignored and
disobeyed their orders and request, then on 26.02.2010 government employees came to the
complainant's premise to demolish only illegal construction and while doing so unlawful

obstructions created by the complainant and his employees due to this act insured has
suffered losses which he is claiming in this complaint so that according to the principle of law
no one can get any insurance indemnification against any loss which occurred due to

unlawful act of himself hence this complaint is liable to be dismissed on this ground only.
12. Learned counsel for the complainant who has also filed written arguments
argued that the complainant is having showroom and workshop at Hoshangabad Road,

Bhopal and the same was insured with the opposite party-insurance company under
different policies. New stock of vehicles, customer's vehicles, electrical installation, furniture,
building, spare parts,
-8-
lubricants, oil, tools, computers, printers and laptops were covered under different policies.
On 06.02.2010 the employees of Municipal Corporation illegally demolished the premises

due to which passenger cars, showroom, laptops and other valuable articles got damaged of
which police complaint was made at Misrod Police Station. The complainant claimed
Rs.41,00,000/- from the insurance company by filing claim along with requisite documents.
13. It is further argued that the premises of the complainant were diverted into
commercial land by the order of SDO T.T.Nagar and Municipal Corporation also approved
the map according to which the construction was raised. The insurance company after

inspecting the premises issued policies. However, the claim made by the complainant was
repudiated by the opposite party-insurance company on the ground that the Municipal
Corporation declared the premises illegal whereas the construction was made lawfully and

as per approved map. The opposite party-insurance company while repudiating the claim
 has committed deficiency in service. It is therefore prayed that the complaint be allowed and
the relief as prayed be granted.
14. Learned counsel for the opposite party-insurance company argued that on
26.02.2010 when the Municipal Corporation was removing the illegal encroachments,
employees of the complainant have unlawfully
-9-
obstructed the legitimate action of the Municipal Corporation and while doing so they used
unlawful measures and not only hurt municipal corporation employees but also damaged

their own premises and perils including the vehicles kept in the premises. It is further argued
that the damages to the insured premise were caused due to complainant's own act and not
due to external means. The damages were caused as an outcome of destroying the illegal

encroachment on the premises which is an outcome of unlawful occupation carried on by
the complainant. Thus, the insurance company is not liable to settle the claim of damages
arising out of an unlawful activity, therefore the claim of the complainant is not genuine and

the opposite party-insurance company has rightly repudiated the claim. There has been no
deficiency in service on part of the opposite party. It is therefore prayed that the complaint be
dismissed.
15.
In support of his submissions, learned counsel for the opposite party-insurance
company has filed a decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal No.11885 (
New India
Assurance Company Limited Vs Rajeshwar Sharma and Ors
) decided on 07.12.2018.
16. Heard and perused the record.
17. The points for determination of deciding this complaint are:-
-10-
1) Whether the opposite party-insurance company has committed deficiency in
 service in repudiating the claim of the complainant?
2) If yes, whether the complainant is entitled to get any relief?
18. It is not disputed between the parties that the insurance policies (Total 6 policies
Annexure C-1 page no.10 to 20) were valid at the time of incident i.e. on 26.02.2010. As per
the case of the complainant on 26.02.2010 the Municipal Corporation illegally demolished

and damaged the premises on account of which insured properties passenger cars, Laptop,
 Refrigerator, Music System, Mobiles, Spare Parts, Lubricants, Oil, tools and other articles
got damaged. As per pleadings of the complainant the aforesaid premises/land was diverted

for commercial purpose as per order of SDO, T.T.Nagar in revenue case no.01/A-2A/08-09
and the Municipal Corporation has given consent, approved the map and gave permission
to raise construction.
19. In view of the above pleadings of the complainant, it is apparent that in the
present case legal dispute involving unauthorized or disputed structures/constructions
where the vehicles and other items were kept is involved. As per case of the complainant

such construction was legal
-11-
whereas from the documents annexed at page 171 to 174 which are letters sent by the

Municipal Corporation the construction was without legally approved plan and legal
permission which made construction unauthorized and therefore it was liable to be
demolished. The document on record i.e. FIR dated 26.02.2010 (Annexure C-2) as well as

FIR filed against the officials and employees of the complainant at page no.175 to 180
indicates that on 26.02.2010 allegedly staff/employees of the complainant attacked the
employees of the Municipal Corporation while they were carrying out their work which

indicates that incident occurred in riot and case under different Sections of
IPC
against the
employees of the complainant was registered.
20. The Surveyor appointed by the opposite party-insurance company in its report

dated 29.03.2010 (Page 251 to 278) has also given its finding that Municipal Corporation
issued various notices about illegal occupation but the complainant failed to take remedial
action against the notices and the evidence show that the complainant's occupation was

unlawful and the damage caused or destruction by lawful authority therefore, the loss fall
under exclusion clause (b) and (c) of the policy. These observations and findings are
supported by the letters of Municipal Corporation dated 17.08.2006, 30.08.2006, 08.08.2008

and 25.02.2010 in
-12-
which the complainant was asked to stop the illegal construction work and to remove illegal
and unauthorized construction. Before demolishing construction a letter dated 25.02.2010

was given to the complainant to remove illegal construction within 24 hours. In this letter (at
page 174) the complainant was informed that in case within 24 hours, illegal construction
was not removed, the said construction will be demolished by using lawful measures.
21. In view of all these documents it is apparent that the damages occurred to the
property of the complainant is an outcome of its own negligent act. All these facts and
documents corroborate the survey report given by the Surveyor N.K.Gupta & Co that due to

complainants unlawful occupation the damages caused to insured properties by the lawful
authority (Municipal Corporation), therefore, the loss falls under exclusion clause of the
policy.
22. In Civil Appeal No.11885/2018 (New India Assurance Co.Ltd. Vs Rajeshwar
Sharma & Ors) decided on 07.12.2018, Hon'ble Apex Court

in paragraph 17 has held that:
"According to the law relating to accidental insurance, Insurers are
 exempt from any liability where the loss is attributable to an excepted clause
 which is inserted ex abundanti
-13-
cautela to make it quite clear to the assured that the policy is not intended to
 cover such losses. In paragraph 22 the court noted that the exclusion was clear
 in exempting the insurer from liability for a loss arising from the destruction of
 property caused by "order of the government or any lawful authority".
Therefore, it has been clearly established by Hon'ble Supreme Court that
destruction by a lawfully constituted authority like Municipal Corporation in this case of the

unlawful activities carried on by the insured are beyond the policy coverage.
23. In this case policy document indicates that Municipal Corporation which is a
lawfully constituted authority demolished the unauthorized construction of the complainant.
Even FIR has been registered against employees of the complainant, the opposite party-
 insurance company has not erred in repudiating the claim of the complainant on the ground
that damages were caused during dispossession/destruction operation by lawful authority

and these operations resulted due to complainant's own unlawful occupation and the loss
caused due to criminal act/riot/mischief in mishap at about 1.30pm on 26.02.2010 and a
case under
Section 294
,
323
,
332
,
427
,
145
,
146
and
147
of IPC has been registered

against employees of the
-14-
complainant, hence the insurance company is not liable to compensate the damages to the
complainant.
24. In view of the above discussion, in considered opinion of this Commission the

complainant has failed to prove deficiency in service or unfair trade practice on part of
opposite party-insurance company.
25. Consequently, this complaint is hereby dismissed. Parties to bear their own

costs.
(Justice Sunita Yadav) (Dr. Monika Malik)
 President Member

 ..................J
 SUNITA YADAV
 PRESIDENT
